exposure: diagnosis of invasive cervical cancer (ICC) during pregnancy or within one year following delivery
diagnosis of in situ adenocarcinoma (ISA) during pregnancy or within one year following delivery
outcome: obstetric outcomes (medical termination of pregnancy, surgery)
cohort: 28 patients (20 with invasive cervical cancer, 8 with in situ adenocarcinoma) diagnosed during pregnancy or within one year post-delivery, who received expert opinion from the Cancer Associe a La Grossesse (CALG) network between 2005 and 2018.
finding: Management of cervical cancer during pregnancy is challenging and is associated with a relatively poor maternal prognosis, necessitating multidisciplinary expert advice.
